Six comments

Evit Gabriel (“For Gabriel” in Breton) was written by Daniel Thonon, a musician and composer who was born in Brussels in 1949 and emigrated to Canada in 1963, where he still resides. He plays a variety of instruments, primarily diatonic accordion and hurdy-gurdy. He’s also an instrument builder, composer, etc.

You can see an image of the sheet music for Evit Gabriel here:

http://www.securenet.net/members/bfournie/images/Part_evit_WEB.jpg

More information on Daniel Thonon at his website:

http://www.danielthonon.com/

Our session plays this tune at a fairly slow, hypnotic pace but it gets played at the local ceilis at a more typical reel pace as well.

It seems to get paired with the Bus Stop Reel and/or Dinky’s Reel. Around here we play it with St. Anne’s, but I’m not sure where that combo originated.

↳ Posted by srt19170 on April 21st, 2008.

Evit Gabriel, X:4

Evit Gabriel (“For Gabriel” in Breton) is the last 2 parts (SCOTTISHE FAST) of the 4 part “Larideau Evit Gabriel” written in Am by accordionist and hurdy-gurdy player Daniel Thonon,

The previous comment’s link its sheet music image is now defunct, but is archived at:
https://web.archive.org/web/20080806233632/http://www.securenet.net/members/bfournie/images/Part_evit_WEB.jpg

He was born in 1949 in Brussels (Belgium). Immigrated to Montreal (Canada) in 1963, and studied at McGill University Faculty of Music. Later moved to Switzerland to study harpsichord and early music at the Conservatory of Music in Geneva, and on to Annecy (France) to produce and perform music with his “Le Concert dans l’œuf” early music group. In 1978 he began to study the music of the Arab/Andaluz tradition in Tlemcen (Algeria). Moved back to Canada St-Marc-sur-Richelieu (Quebec) where he still lives. Played with Ensemble Claude Gervaise and Ad Vielle Que Pourra, which disbanded in 1999; after which he formed the group Montcorbier. He composes and arranges for other artists, tours as soloist primarily on the diatonic accordion and baroque hurdy-gurdy, and pursues his various activities in musicology and instrument building.

↳ Posted by Teaticket on July 15th, 2024.

Re: Evit Gabriel

What most people call “Evit Gabriel” is the last 2 parts of the original tune “Larideau Evit Gabriel” (written in Key of Am) and transposed to Key of Em.

This was the first tune setting I posted to The Session, and somehow the quote marks on the Chords were changed to some form of ‘smart quotes’ which were ignored, changing the Chord names to the corresponding notes (e.g. E7 became a half note with 2 dots, making it in between a dotted half note and a whole note). ABC software rightfully ignores what it doesn’t understand, instead of crashing - in this case leading to some odd extra notes.

I’ve fixed the ‘stupid quotes’ in X:4.

X:5 corrected the ‘smart quotes’ AND transposed it to Key of Em.

↳ Posted by Teaticket on July 21st, 2024.
